items.rationale: Theft peril applies; frame was genuinely damaged in the theft (2.3.1(b)), so repair/replacement is indemnifiable as a necessary repair cost (7.1.1(b), 7.1.7(b)). Subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit (4.2.2), rateably across all indemnifiable lines in this class. Reference Case 24: t between 142 and 349 for frame replacement.

Brakes were genuinely damaged in the theft (2.3.1(b)), so repair/replacement is indemnifiable as a necessary repair cost (7.1.1(b), 7.1.7(b)). Subject to the EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit, rateably. Reference Case 24: t between 130 and 148 for brake replacement.
Tracker was not itself damaged or taken in the theft; replacement is an elective purchase and not indemnifiable (3.1.7, 7.1.8(b)).
Second bike was not affected by the theft; service is maintenance and not indemnifiable (3.1.6, 7.1.8(a), 7.1.5).
Helmet and lights were not affected items; these are new accessories purchased after the event and not indemnifiable (3.1.7, 7.1.8(b)).
Shipping is indemnifiable only if it relates to the repair/recovery of the affected bike (7.1.7(f)). Reference Case 24: t between 24 and 27. Subject to sub-limit and rateable reduction.

Vehicle costs are ancillary and indemnifiable only if they relate to the repair/recovery of the affected bike (7.1.7(g)). Reference Case 24: t below 27, possibly 0, but Case 34: t >= 76 for vehicle costs. Given context, moderate estimate and subject to sub-limit.
Assembly costs are indemnifiable as part of the repair of the affected bike (7.1.7(c)). Reference Case 24: t between 106 and 209, but subject to sub-limit and rateable reduction.
Miscellaneous items are only indemnifiable if they are small parts/sundries consumed in the repair of the affected bike (7.1.7(e)). Reference Case 24: t below 8, possibly 0.
Labour hours are indemnifiable if they relate to the repair of the affected bike (7.1.7(d)). Reference Case 24: t below 18, possibly 0.
Labour hours are indemnifiable if they relate to the repair of the affected bike (7.1.7(d)). Reference Case 24: t between 35 and 42.
Recovery cost under 5.2.2(a); necessary to recover the stolen bike. Reference Case 24: t below 35, possibly 0, but Case 26: t below 35, possibly 0. Given necessity, moderate estimate.

items.description: Cut and remove seized lock to release bicycle
items.rationale: Recovery cost under 5.2.2(b); necessary to recover the stolen bike. Reference Case 26: t >= 99 for 2 pcs.
Ancillary recovery cost, only indemnifiable if required for the recovery (7.1.7(g), 5.2.2(a)). Reference Case 24: t below 30, possibly 0.

items.description: Impound release / storage fee paid to recover bicycle
items.rationale: Explicitly covered as a recovery cost under 5.2.2(c); charge required by third party for release of recovered item. Capped by EUR 1,000 recovery limit and EUR 500 mobility equipment sub-limit.
Explicitly excluded under 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d); not indemnifiable.
Labour hours are indemnifiable if they relate to the recovery of the affected bike (7.1.7(d), 5.2.2(b)). Reference Case 24: t below 18, possibly 0.
Labour hours are indemnifiable if they relate to the recovery of the affected bike (7.1.7(d), 5.2.2(b)). Reference Case 24: t between 35 and 42.
